facts.title: Country and period
facts.text: Country: Namibia (NAM). Annual period 2014–2025, monthly series 2014-01-01 → 2025-12-01. Levels: ADM1, ADM2. Synthetic data: no.

facts.title: National trend
facts.text: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in Namibia changed by +5.6% per year (95% CI: +4.1% to +6.4%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is -1.6% relative to the previous 12 months. (confidence high: significant trend (p < 0.01; n = 12))

facts.title: Regions
facts.text: Of 103 ADM2 units, 87 show significant growth, 16 are stagnating and 0 are declining. Light remains concentrated: Erongo accounts for 17% of national light. (confidence medium: classification of 103 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10)

facts.title: Convergence
facts.text: Across ADM2 units, light per capita converges: the least-lit units are catching up. (confidence medium: β = −0.033 [−0.045; −0.020], n = 103)

facts.title: Link with GDP
facts.text: The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 1.85 in levels (95% CI: −0.48 to 4.17, R² = 0.22, 12 years) and −0.24 in growth rates (CI: −0.82 to 0.33). Out of sample, light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.55 (mean absolute error: 3.6 percentage points of growth). (confidence low: n = 12, not significant (p = 0.12))

facts.title: Shocks
facts.text: The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of -2.9% (03/2021), return to the pre-shock level after 13 months. (confidence low: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability)

facts.title: Inequality and access
facts.text: The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.44 in 2025 (significant decrease since 2014). About 0.01 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (17% of the inhabited population). (confidence medium: sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.01 to 0.01 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection)

facts.title: Industrial zones
facts.text: 45 industrial clusters detected from concordant satellite signals: 10 heavy industry, 10 business parks & logistics, 8 oil & gas sites and 17 isolated sites to verify. They emit 17.8% of national light (latest year); their light changes by +2.0% per year. Oshana has the most industrial activity. (confidence low: precision 51% and recall 14% against the reference list)

facts.title: Summer tourism
facts.text: 4 of 103 units show a net summer light excess of at least 10%: Otavi (Oshana), Ongenga (Ohangwena), Aminius (Ohangwena), Tsumkwe (Kunene). The median net excess reaches +17% in the most touristic zone. The season index (base 100 = 2019) falls to 309 in 2020 and stands at 266 in 2025. (confidence low: correlation of -0.13 with international tourist arrivals (WDI) (7 years))

facts.title: Urbanisation
facts.text: The lit area changes by +11.0% per year, against +1.7% for population. Of 103 ADM2 units: 86 show electrified urbanisation, 7 balanced growth, 7 unlit growth. Between 2014 and 2025, 2,678 km² became lit, of which 30 km² in already inhabited areas (≈ 1k newly lit inhabitants). Largest expansion: Walvisbay Urban (Khomas), Soweto (Erongo), Khomasdal North (Erongo). (confidence high: rank correlation of 0.71 with GHSL built-up growth (103 units))

facts.title: Key indicators
facts.text: Annual growth of light = +5.6% (2014–2025, robust slope (Theil–Sen)); Last 12 months vs previous 12 = -1.6% (seasonally adjusted series, up to 12/2025); Light–GDP elasticity = 1.85 (95% CI −0.48 to 4.17 · confidence low); Gini of light per capita = 0.44 (ADM2 units, 2025); People in the dark = 0.01 M (17% of the inhabited population, 2025); Share of the top region = 17% (Erongo, 2025); Industrial clusters = 45 (18% of national light); Tourist zones = 4 (max. summer excess +17% (Otavi (Oshana))); Lit area = +11.0% (annual growth; population +1.7%/yr)

facts.title: Recommendations
facts.text: • Use night-time lights as a leading and subnational indicator, as a complement to — never a replacement for — the national accounts. • Do not disseminate light-based GDP estimates: the NTL–GDP relationship is not established with sufficient confidence over this period. • Cross-check the map of populations “in the dark” against grid-connection registers: the average gap with the World Bank access rate is +29 percentage points. • Document breaks detected without an associated event (sensor change, outage, local event) before any economic interpretation. • Have the 17 isolated sites checked on high-resolution imagery and complete the official register of industrial zones used as the validation reference. • Monitor the light of industrial clusters monthly as a leading indicator of industrial output, and compare it with the industrial production index where one exists. • Publish the tourist season index right after the summer (VIIRS data are available within weeks), ahead of hotel-night statistics, and recalibrate it on them every year. • Cross newly lit areas with urban plans and grid-connection registers to tell planned expansion, informal settlements and rural electrification apart. • Prioritise infrastructure (power grid, services) where population grows faster than the lit area: Mariental Rural (Karas), Windhoek East (Khomas), Epupa (Khomas), Khorixas (Khomas). • Update the dashboard every quarter (monthly VIIRS series) and every year (annual VNL composites).

facts.title: Limitation: What lights measure
facts.text: Upward radiance emitted around 01:30: agriculture, daytime trade, poorly lit services and the rural informal economy are poorly captured.

facts.title: Limitation: Saturation and blooming
facts.text: DMSP saturates in city centres (DN 63) and “blooms” beyond lit areas; VIIRS is much better, but blooming still inflates the lit area of cities.

facts.title: Limitation: Gas flares and isolated sites
facts.text: The automatic mask may remove isolated mines, ports or power plants, and miss small flares; candidates are exported for verification.

facts.title: Limitation: Clouds, seasons, moon
facts.text: Cloudy months are only partially observed; STL removes average seasonality but not an abnormal season (snow, late monsoon).

facts.title: Limitation: Product breaks
facts.text: DMSP and VIIRS are not directly comparable: the harmonised long series (Li et al., 2020) is a modelled product, to be read for trends only.

facts.title: Limitation: NTL–GDP elasticity
facts.text: Estimated on 10 to 30 annual observations: wide intervals, possible instability, a non-causal relationship that varies with the level of development.

facts.title: Limitation: Access to electricity
facts.text: “Inhabited without light” ≠ “not connected”: a connected household with low consumption is invisible; the indicator depends strongly on the radiance threshold and the population data.

facts.title: Limitation: Administrative boundaries
facts.text: geoBoundaries/GAUL may differ from official boundaries; small ADM2 units are sensitive to light spilling over from neighbouring units.

facts.title: Limitation: Industrial zones
facts.text: Detection relies on thresholds: a power plant, a port or a large shopping centre can meet the signals; a dimly lit factory without visible emissions is missed. Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) are coarser than VIIRS: NO₂/SO₂/heat signals describe a neighbourhood, not a building.

facts.title: Limitation: Summer tourism
facts.text: The summer excess captures any rise in summer light (second homes, diaspora visits, festivals, construction), not only tourism; at high latitudes, very short summer nights reduce VIIRS observations. Ramadan changes night-time activity: the summers concerned are flagged.

facts.title: Limitation: Urbanisation
facts.text: The lit area depends on the detection threshold and on light blooming around cities; a connected but dimly lit neighbourhood stays invisible. Population (GHSL/WorldPop) is modelled from censuses: its growth is not an independent observation, and years between two epochs are interpolated.

facts.title: ADM2: ranking
facts.text: 103 ADM2 units. Classes: Growth 87, Stagnation 16. Fastest growth: Ndiyona (Oshikoto) (+26.9%), Okongo (Omusati) (+25.0%), Steinhausen (Oshana) (+24.8%), Ohangwena (Oshana) (+24.5%), Kalahari (Ohangwena) (+23.4%), Ondangwa (Oshikoto) (+20.3%), Mpungu (Oshikoto) (+19.1%), Okatyali (Oshikoto) (+19.0%). Slowest: Luderitz (Oshikoto) (-2.2%), Katutura East (Hardap) (-1.7%), Walvisbay Rural (Hardap) (-1.4%), Windhoek Rural (Khomas) (-0.6%), Khorixas (Khomas) (-0.3%), Mariental Rural (Karas) (+0.1%), Okakarara (Khomas) (+0.1%), Eenhana (Khomas) (+0.2%).

facts.title: ADM2: brightest
facts.text: Brightest units: Walvisbay Urban (Khomas) (4.6%), Outjo (Erongo) (4.3%), Soweto (Erongo) (4.0%), Windhoek Rural (Khomas) (3.1%), Kalahari (Oshana) (3.1%), Khomasdal North (Erongo) (3.0%), Onesi (Oshana) (2.8%), Otjinene (Oshana) (2.8%), Kahenge (Otjozondjupa) (2.5%), Windhoek West (Khomas) (2.4%).

facts.title: Convergence and concentration
facts.text: β-convergence (ADM2): β = -0.033 (CI -0.045 to -0.020, n = 103). β < 0 with a fully negative CI = convergence. Share of the leading region: 23.2% in 2014 → 16.7% in 2025; HHI 0.105.

facts.title: Elasticity (levels)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in levels: β = 1.85 (95% CI -0.48 to 4.17, R² = 0.22, n = 12, confidence low: n = 12, not significant (p = 0.12)). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (growth rates)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in growth rates: β = -0.24 (95% CI -0.82 to 0.33, R² = 0.03, n = 11, confidence low: n = 11, not significant (p = 0.41)). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (long DMSP–VIIRS series)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in long DMSP–VIIRS series: β = 0.85 (95% CI 0.59 to 1.10, R² = 0.92, n = 30, confidence high: n = 30, p < 0.01, narrow CI). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Out-of-sample tracking
facts.text: Out of sample, light-based growth has a correlation of -0.55 with official growth; mean absolute error 3.6 percentage point.

facts.title: Shock: COVID-19
facts.text: COVID-19 (2020-03-01 → 2021-06-30): trough of -2.9% on 2021-03-01, back to the pre-shock level after 13 months. Distinguishable from noise: no.

facts.title: Detected breaks
facts.text: Structural breaks: 2017-01-01 (13.4 %); 2023-02-01 (11.6 %). Without a known event within ±6 months: 2.

facts.title: Regional impact of shocks
facts.text: Hardest-hit regions (trough): Hardap -30.0 % (covid19), Khomas -26.6 % (covid19), Omaheke -22.7 % (covid19), Erongo -16.9 % (covid19), Otjozondjupa -15.0 % (covid19).

facts.title: Gini and Theil
facts.text: Gini of light per capita (ADM2): 0.533 in 2014 → 0.442 in 2025 (change -0.091, bootstrap CI -0.142 to -0.049). Theil T 0.332; between-region share 33%.

facts.title: Population in the dark
facts.text: People in inhabited areas without detectable light: 0.01 M (19%) in 2014 → 0.01 M (17%) in 2025. Urban/rural light-per-capita ratio 0.7. Proxy of electricity access, sensitive to the threshold.

facts.title: Comparison with the World Bank
facts.text: Average gap between the share of people in lit areas and the World Bank electricity-access rate: 28.9 points.

facts.title: Industrial zones: summary
facts.text: 45 industrial clusters (≥ 3 of 6 signals): Isolated site to verify 17, Heavy industry 10, Business park & logistics 10, Oil, gas & flares 8. Share of national light: 17.8%; annual growth +2.0%. Validation (OpenStreetMap): precision 51%, recall 14%.

facts.title: Urbanisation: lit area and population
facts.text: National lit area: +11.0% per year; population: +1.7% per year. Classes (ADM2): Electrified urbanisation 86, Balanced growth 7, Unlit growth 7, Stable or declining 3.

facts.title: Urbanisation: newly lit areas
facts.text: Between 2014 and 2025: 2,678 km² newly lit, of which 30 km² already inhabited (electrification, ≈ 1k people) and 2,648 km² of new settlements; 71 km² lost their light.

facts.title: Urbanisation: units
facts.text: Fastest lit-area expansion: Outapi (Oshana) (+39.2%/yr), Oshikuku (Oshana) (+35.9%/yr), Kalahari (Ohangwena) (+33.9%/yr), Okongo (Omusati) (+32.7%/yr), Okalongo (Oshana) (+31.0%/yr), Epembe (Omusati) (+30.4%/yr). Unlit growth (population faster than light): Mariental Rural (Karas), Windhoek East (Khomas), Epupa (Khomas), Khorixas (Khomas), Opuwo (Erongo), Eenhana (Khomas), Okakarara (Khomas).

facts.title: Validation with GHSL built-up
facts.text: Spearman rank correlation between lit-area growth and GHSL built-up growth: 0.71 (p = 0.000, 103 units).

facts.title: Quality and international standards
facts.text: Night-time-light indicators are experimental statistics: they complement official statistics and do not replace them. Every output is published with its method, validation, uncertainty, limitations and a confidence level. Frameworks applied: UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics, DQAF, UNECE GSBPM, FAIR principles.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Time dynamics
facts.text: Validation: Trend significance (Mann–Kendall) and monthly/annual consistency (p-value = < 0.0001). Uncertainty: 95% CI of annual growth: +4.1% to +6.4% Limitations: Cloud cover and short summer nights; light is not value added. Status: experimental statistic; confidence high.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Regional growth and convergence
facts.text: Validation: Rank correlation with tropospheric NO₂ (independent source) (Spearman ρ = -0.21). Uncertainty: Class assigned only if |slope| ≥ threshold and p < α; CI of β (robust errors). Limitations: Small units: noise and light blooming between neighbours. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Light–GDP relationship
facts.text: Validation: Out-of-sample tracking of official growth (correlation / MAE (pp) = -0.55 / 3.6). Uncertainty: 95% CI of the elasticity: -0.48 to 4.17; 80% and 95% prediction intervals. Limitations: Short annual sample; regional GDP is an experimental statistic to be checked against regional accounts. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Shocks and resilience
facts.text: Validation: Does the trough exceed ordinary variability? (trough (main shock) = -2.9% — no). Uncertainty: Pre-shock month-to-month variability (robust SD); unexplained breaks flagged. Limitations: Shocks hitting poorly lit activities (agriculture, daytime services) are underestimated. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Inequality and electrification
facts.text: Validation: Gap with the World Bank electricity-access rate (mean gap (pp) = 28.9). Uncertainty: Range across radiance thresholds; bootstrap CI of the Gini. Limitations: Proxy of outdoor lighting, not of connection: a connected but dimly lit household looks “in the dark”. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Industrial zones
facts.text: Validation: Comparison with the reference list (OpenStreetMap) (precision / recall / F1 = 51% / 14% / 0.22). Uncertainty: Per-cluster confidence from the number of strong signals; isolated sites to verify. Limitations: Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) resolution: signals describe a neighbourhood. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Seasonal tourism
facts.text: Validation: Correlation with international tourist arrivals (WDI) (r = -0.13). Uncertainty: p-value per unit; 2020–2021 excluded from the classification. Limitations: Any summer activity (diaspora, second homes, festivals) is captured, not only tourism. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Urbanisation signals
facts.text: Validation: Rank correlation with GHSL built-up area growth (independent source) (Spearman ρ = 0.71). Uncertainty: Persistence required over two years to limit noise; ± 1 pp margin between growth rates before classifying. Limitations: Light measures outdoor lighting, not urbanisation in the administrative sense; blooming widens cities; GHSL population is interpolated between epochs. Status: experimental statistic; confidence high.

facts.title: Method — Method
facts.text: Data: VIIRS DNB monthly (VCMSLCFG) and annual VNL V2, harmonised DMSP–VIIRS, daily Black Marble, GHSL/WorldPop, Sentinel-5P NO₂/SO₂, MODIS LST, World Bank. Cleaning: pixels valid if cf_cvg ≥ 2, unit-month kept if ≥ 80% of pixels observed, spikes replaced, background and gas flares masked.

facts.title: Method — Dynamics
facts.text: Dynamics: robust STL on log(sum of lights), Theil–Sen trend + Mann–Kendall test, year-on-year growth, breaks by piecewise-linear segmentation with a BIC penalty.

facts.title: Method — Regions
facts.text: Regions: robust growth per unit, Growth/Decline class if |slope| ≥ 1%/yr and p < 0.10; β-convergence (robust OLS), σ-convergence, Herfindahl index.

facts.title: Method — GDP
facts.text: GDP: log(NTL) = α + β log(GDP) in levels and growth rates, HAC standard errors, DW/BP/JB diagnostics, out-of-sample tracking; experimental regional GDP allocated by light (γ = 1 and 0.5).

facts.title: Method — Shocks
facts.text: Shocks: trough = largest gap to the 12-month pre-shock level of the seasonally adjusted series, recovery = return to that level; daily Black Marble index (7-day rolling median).

facts.title: Method — Inequality
facts.text: Inequality: population-weighted Gini, Theil (between/within decomposition) and Lorenz; population in the dark = residents of pixels ≥ 5 people below 0.5 nW (sensitivity 0.25/0.5/1).

facts.title: Method — Industry
facts.text: Industry: six signals per pixel (light ≥ 5 nW, light per resident, GHSL non-residential built-up, Sentinel-5P NO₂ and SO₂, MODIS surface heat); pixels with ≥ 3 signals grouped into clusters; typology, confidence from concordant signals, precision/recall validation (official list or OSM).

facts.title: Method — Tourism
facts.text: Tourism: summer excess = log(peak-month light / shoulder-month light); net of the median of comparable units at the same latitude; tourist zone if ≥ +10% and significant over ≥ 3 summers; season index base 100; Ramadan flagged; validation with hotel nights.

facts.title: Method — Urbanisation
facts.text: Urbanisation: annual lit area (pixels ≥ threshold) and its growth (Theil–Sen) compared with population growth (GHSL/WorldPop); newly lit areas (dark in the first 2 years, lit in the last 2), split into electrification of already inhabited areas and new settlements; validation with GHSL BUILT-S built-up growth.

tools.name: search_facts
tools.description: Search the published facts (key messages, methods, limitations, national figures) for those answering a question. Use it first for any general question.

tools.name: rank_units
tools.description: Rank regions (ADM1) or districts (ADM2) by an indicator for the latest year: fastest growth, largest share of population in the dark, etc.

tools.name: unit_profile
tools.description: Full profile of a region or district: latest indicators, light trend, growth class, industrial and tourist zones.

tools.name: compare_units
tools.description: Compare several units (or the country) on an annual indicator between two years: levels, change and compound annual growth rate.

tools.name: make_chart
tools.description: Draw a chart (annual series of an indicator for units, or a ranking bar chart) shown in the conversation.

tools.name: map_action
tools.description: Drive the dashboard's interactive map: show a year, compare two years (swipe), focus on a unit, or show a layer (lights, population in the dark, indicator, industrial clusters, tourist zones).
